inlines.v: DIFFUSE, verb transitive diffuze. [Latin , to pour, to spread.] 1. To pour out and spread, as a fluid; to cause to flow and spread. The river rose and diffused its waters over the adjacent plain. 2. To spread; to send out or extend in all directions; to disperse. Flowers diffuse their odors. The fame of Washington is diffused over Europe. The knowledge of the true God will be diffused over the earth. DIFFUSE, adjective 1. Widely spread; dispersed. 2. Copious; prolix; using many words; giving full descriptions; as, Livy is a diffuse writer. 3. Copious; verbose; containing full or particular accounts; concise; as a diffuse style.
